label: thm:euclidean-small
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:euclidean-small}
There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\geq1$ and
$1\leq k\leq n/2$,
\[
   {\rm povr}_k(B_2^n)\leq C.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L\subset{\mathbb R}^n$ be a convex body.  Fix an orthogonal projection $P$ of
rank $2k$ and put $E=P{\mathbb R}^n$.  We regard $PL$ as a convex body in the
$2k$-dimensional Euclidean space $E$.

Applying Theorem~6.1 of \cite{GLMP} in the space $E$, with $\lambda=1/2$, we 
find orthogonal projections $S,T:E\to E$ of rank $k$ such that
\[
   {\rm vr}(SPL,TB_2^{2k})\leq C.
\]
Since $S$ and $T$ are orthogonal projections onto subspaces of $E$, the
operators $SP$ and $TP$ are orthogonal projections of ${\mathbb R}^n$ of rank $k$.
Moreover, $TB_2^{2k}$ is a Euclidean ball in its range and hence isometric to
$B_2^k$.  Therefore
\[
   \inf_{U,V}{\rm vr}(UL,VB_2^n)\leq C,
\]
where the infimum is over all rank $k$ orthogonal projections $U,V$.
Taking the supremum over $L$ proves the result.
head: environment

label: thm:general-small
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:general-small}
There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that for every convex body
$K\subset{\mathbb R}^n$,
\[
   {\rm povr}_k(K)\leq C, \qquad 1\leq k\leq c\ln n,
\]
and
\[
   {\rm povr}_k(K)\leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}},
   \qquad c\ln n\leq k\leq n/2.
\]
head: environment

label: eq:L-eucl
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a convex body $L\subset{\mathbb R}^n$.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:euclidean-small}
there is a rank $k$ orthogonal projection $P$ such that, after identifying its
range with ${\mathbb R}^k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:L-eucl}
   {\rm vr}(PL,B_2^k)\leq C.
\end{equation}

If $1\leq k\leq c\ln n$, Dvoretzky's theorem (see e.g. \cite{AGM-book}) 
applied to $K$ gives a rank $k$ projection $Q$ which is at an absolute distance from $B_2^k$.
Together with \eqref{eq:L-eucl}, and the multiplicative inequality for the
volume ratio (see e.g. \cite[Fact~2.1]{GLMP}), this gives
\[
   {\rm vr}(PL,QK)\leq C,
\]
which proves  \({\rm povr}_k(K)\leq C\).

Assume now that $c\ln n\leq k\leq n/2$.  The isomorphic Dvoretzky theorem
for projections gives a rank $k$ orthogonal projection $Q$ and an affine
image of $QK$, which we again denote by $QK$, such that for some $a, b>0$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:K-eucl}
   \frac{1}{b} B_2^k\subset QK\subset a B_2^k,
   \qquad
   ab \leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}}.
\end{equation}
Therefore
\[
   {\rm vr}(B_2^k,QK)\leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}}.
\]
Using again the multiplicative inequality for the volume ratio and
\eqref{eq:L-eucl},
\[
\begin{split}
   {\rm vr}(PL,QK)
   &\leq {\rm vr}(PL,B_2^k)\,{\rm vr}(B_2^k,QK) \leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}}.
\end{split}
\]
Taking the infimum over $P,Q$ and then the supremum over $L$ proves the
theorem.
head: environment

label: prop:B1-sharp
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:B1-sharp}
There are absolute constants $c,C,c_0>0$ such that
\[
 c\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}}
 \leq {\rm povr}_k(B_1^n)
 \leq C\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}},
 \qquad c_0\ln n\leq k\leq n/2.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The upper estimate follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:general-small}.  For the
lower estimate, choose $L=B_2^n$ in \eqref{eq:def-povr}.  Thus
\[
 {\rm povr}_k(B_1^n)
 \geq \inf_{\operatorname{rank}Q=k}{\rm vr}(B_2^k,QB_1^n).
\]
Fix such a projection $Q$.  Let $T$ be an affine map satisfying
$T(QB_1^n)\subset B_2^k$.  Since both bodies are symmetric, we can assume that $T$
is linear.
Set $w_i=TQe_i$, $1\leq i\leq n$.  Then $\|w_i\|_2\leq1$ and
\[
   T(QB_1^n)={\rm absconv}\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}.
\]
The standard volume bound (see \cite{BF,CP,Gl}) yields 
\[
   |T(QB_1^n)|^{1/k}
   \leq C\frac{\sqrt{\ln(2n/k)}}{k}.
\]
Since $|B_2^k|^{1/k}\asymp k^{-1/2}$,
\[
 \left(\frac{|B_2^k|}{|T(QB_1^n)|}\right)^{1/k}
 \geq c\sqrt{\frac{k}{\ln(2n/k)}}.
\]
This proves the lower bound.
head: environment

label: lem:sym-reduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sym-reduction}
Let $K\subset{\mathbb R}^n$ be a symmetric convex body and let $1\leq k<n$.
Then
\[
 {\rm povr}^{s}_k(K)\leq{\rm povr}_k(K)
 \leq \left(2^n{n\choose k}\right)^{1/k}{\rm povr}^{s}_k(K).
\]
In particular, if $k>n/2$, then
\[
   {\rm povr}_k(K)\leq16\,{\rm povr}^{s}_k(K).
\]
head: environment

label: eq:MP
title: Proof
body_md:
The first inequality and the ``in particular part'' are trivial. 

 Let $L\subset{\mathbb R}^n$ be an arbitrary
convex body.  Translating $L$ if necessary, we may assume that its centroid
is the origin.  Set
\[
   L_0=L\cap(-L).
\]
By the Milman--Pajor inequality \cite[Corollary 3]{MP},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:MP}
   |L_0|\geq2^{-n}|L|.
\end{equation}

Let $P$ be an orthogonal projection of rank $k$ and let $E=P{\mathbb R}^n$. By the 
Fubini theorem,
\[
 |L_0|\leq |PL_0|\,
 \max_{x\in E}|L_0\cap(x+E^\perp)|.
\]
Since $L_0\subset L$, the Rogers--Shephard  inequality
\cite{RS} yields
\[
 |L_0|
 \leq |PL_0|{n\choose k}\frac{|L|}{|PL|}.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:MP}, this implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:projection-sym}
 \left(\frac{|PL|}{|PL_0|}\right)^{1/k}
 \leq \left(2^n{n\choose k}\right)^{1/k}.
\end{equation}

Fix rank $k$ projections $P,Q$.  Since $PL_0$ and $QK$ are symmetric, the
affine map in the definition of ${\rm vr}(PL_0,QK)$ may be replaced by its linear
part.  Consequently the same image of $QK$ which is contained in $PL_0$ is
also contained in $PL$.  By \eqref{eq:projection-sym},
\[
 {\rm vr}(PL,QK)
 \leq \left(2^n{n\choose k}\right)^{1/k}{\rm vr}(PL_0,QK).
\]
Taking the infimum over $P,Q$ and then the supremum over $L$ proves the
second inequality.

label: thm:ABBP
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Alonso-Guti\'errez--Bastero--Bernu\'es--Paouris

label: thm:euclidean-large
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove the upper estimate.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:sym-reduction}, it is enough to 
consider only symmetric bodies $L$ under the supremum.
For every such $L$, Theorem~\ref{thm:ABBP} provides a rank $k$
projection $P$ with
\[
 {\rm vr}(PL,B_2^k)
 \leq C\sqrt{\frac{n}{n-k}}
 \ln\left(1+\frac{n}{n-k}\right).
\]
Every rank $k$ orthogonal projection of $B_2^n$ is a Euclidean ball in its
range, so the upper estimate follows directly from the definition of
${\rm povr}_k(B_2^n)$.

For the lower estimate, take $L=B_\infty^n$ in the definition of
${\rm povr}_k(B_2^n)$.  Since every rank $k$ projection of $B_2^n$ is a Euclidean
ball in its range,
\[
 {\rm povr}_k(B_2^n)
 \geq \inf_{\operatorname{rank}P=k}{\rm vr}(PB_\infty^n,B_2^k).
\]
The body $PB_\infty^n$ is the unit ball of a $k$-dimensional quotient of
$\ell_\infty^n$.  The classical small-codimension estimates for quotients of
$\ell_\infty^n$ imply
\[
 \inf_{\operatorname{rank}P=k}{\rm vr}(PB_\infty^n,B_2^k)
 \geq c\sqrt{\frac{n}{n-k}};
\]
see \cite{GTJ,GMP,GJ} and the references therein.  This proves the lower
estimate and completes the proof.
head: environment
